question: The housing crisis in Europe is being worsened by the pressure of short-term tourist rentals on the residential stock, reducing the supply available to residents and driving up access costs; in cities such as Barcelona, thousands of tourist rental licences have been withdrawn to return homes to residential use. 1.

Given that the Commission is preparing the first European housing plan in the light of the new EU regulation on short-term accommodation rentals, does the Commission intend to include in that plan binding measures on tourist rentals in ‘tensioned areas’ – areas officially designated as experiencing significant pressure in the housing rental market, including high housing costs relative to local incomes – which would allow Member States and cities to limit them with legal certainty and EU support?

If so, what concrete coordination and support mechanisms does the Commission intend to provide to support cities that are already regulating or restricting tourist rentals in areas facing a housing crisis?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.7.2026) Short-term rentals offer many benefits: greater choice, and a boost to tourism, incomes and jobs. While the shortage of affordable housing can mainly be attributed to other structural factors, increases in short term rental activity have been associated with higher rental and sale prices in several European cities.
1 In December 2025, the Commission adopted the European Affordable Housing Plan2 setting ten key areas of action where the EU can add value and support Member States in addressing the housing crisis.

Among these actions, the Commission will propose an Affordable Housing Act in 2026, to help public authorities identify areas under housing stress, using publicly available data, and enable them, in line with subsidiarity, to take proportionate measures to safeguard housing availability and affordability in those areas.

The Commission is currently assessing different policy options to support local decision-making and to increase legal certainty, while fully respecting the competence of authorities in the Member States in matters of housing policy.

Moreover, the Regulation on Short-term Rentals3 which has been applicable since 20 May 2026 will bring more transparency and help public authorities to design appropriate policies by providing for harmonised rules on the registration of hosts and sharing of activity data between digital platforms and national authorities.

1 Commission Staff Working Document accompanying the EAHP “Understanding the Housing Crisis”. 2 The European Affordable Housing Action Plan. COM (2025) 1025 final. 3 Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on data collection
and sharing relating to short-term accommodation rental services and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 OJ L, 2024/1028, 29.4.2024.
